Seminar Title:

Analysis of Fractal Functions Corresponding to Linear and Non-linear Iterated Function Systems

Abstract:

Fractal geometry provides a framework for constructing complex and self-similar structures, with iterated function systems (IFSs) forming a central foundation. An IFS typically consists of a finite set of contraction mappings acting on a complete metric space. The fractal interpolation functions (FIFs) with appropriate IFSs provide a method to perturb and approximate a continuous function on a compact interval. This seminar provides a comprehensive framework for fractal interpolation and approximation using generalized IFSs, with particular emphasis on non-stationary dynamics, recurrent constructions, and weak IFSs on fractal domains. The primary objective is to extend classical stationary fractal interpolation theory by introducing greater flexibility in operator selection while maintaining rigorous analytical, stability, and dimensional properties. After establishing the necessary preliminaries and stationary foundations, the thesis first investigates non-stationary &alpha-fractal functions generated by sequences of contractive operators. These constructions generalize classical stationary interpolants and enable improved approximation of non-smooth functions. The associated fractal operators are studied on spaces of continuous, Lipschitz, bounded variation, convex Lipschitz, Hӧlder, and higher-order differentiable functions. Key topological properties are analyzed, and stability under perturbations, sensitivity with respect to IFS parameters, continuous dependence, and explicit upper bounds for approximation errors are established. Dimensional properties of the resulting non-stationary fractal interpolants are also examined. Next these works are extended to the multivariate settings. Recurrent fractal interpolation function (RFIF) is a generalization of FIF which provides an efficient way to reconstruct data that presents self-affinity in a piecewise form. The thesis develops a recurrent fractal interpolation framework based on weak IFSs. Using Edelstein contractions, a general construction of RFIFs is presented, significantly broadening the admissible class of interpolants beyond classical contractive settings. Lower and upper bounds for the box dimension of the graphs of nonlinear RFIFs are derived by extending existing techniques for self-affine fractals, demonstrating the effectiveness of recurrent structures in modeling piecewise self-affine data. Finally, the theory is extended to weak IFS-based fractal interpolation on the Sierpiǹski gasket, a prototypical post-critically finite fractal. Nonlinear fractal interpolation functions are constructed within a generalized Edelstein contraction framework, and their graphs are characterized as unique attractors of the associated IFSs. Conditions for Lebesgue integrability are obtained, and estimates for the Hausdorff and box dimensions of the graphs are derived using analytical properties of harmonic functions on the gasket. Overall, this thesis unifies non-stationary, recurrent, and weak IFS-based fractal interpolation within a single analytical framework, contributing new results to approximation theory and fractal geometry on both Euclidean and fractal domains.
